The Brake Not Set warning remains active or changes intermittently. The display reports the wrong brake position. Do not bypass, defeat, or electrically simulate the brake sensor to keep the bed in service. Expected outcome: The failure category is identified sufficiently for safe escalation and work order documentation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Hillrom Progressa continued to display and sound a Brake Not Set warning after the brake pedal was engaged.
CCR.Cause: Brake pedal and casters engaged mechanically, but the brake-status indication remained active during repeated testing, indicating a probable brake-position sensor or associated wiring failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the bed from service, applied an Out of Service label, and routed it for authorized brake sensor and linkage evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Visible cable or connector damage noted
Fluid exposure, unusual heat, or odor noted
Out of Service label applied when required

title: Hillrom Progressa Hospital Bed - Head, Knee, or Foot Actuator Not Moving
description: Troubleshooting a bed section that will not move due to lockouts, controls, obstructions, power loss, mechanical binding, or actuator-related failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot bed articulation while supporting an unstable, unmonitored, or procedure-dependent patient. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Transfer the patient to another approved bed when continued positioning capability is clinically necessary. Secure all lines, tubes, drains, cables, and accessories before attempting bed movement. Keep hands, feet, equipment, and patient extremities away from moving frame sections and pinch points. Do not attempt to force a section into position manually. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from unintended movement, entrapment, line disruption, or loss of required positioning. If the affected movement is needed for immediate patient care, remove the bed from clinical use rather than continuing troubleshooting with the patient aboard.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Movement Has Failed
steps.instructions: Identify the exact complaint: Head section will not raise or lower. Knee section will not raise or lower. Foot section will not articulate or retract as expected. Movement works in only one direction. Movement starts and stops intermittently. The section moves from one control location but not another. Multiple bed movements are inoperative. Test only when the bed is unloaded or when Clinical Engineering has confirmed that testing with the patient present is safe. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a specific section, direction, control location, or broader bed-function problem.

steps.title: 3. Check the Caregiver Control Lockouts
steps.instructions: Inspect the caregiver control panel for an enabled articulation lockout. Verify whether the head, knee, foot, or general bed-position controls are locked. Disable the applicable lockout in accordance with facility policy. Test the affected function from the caregiver controls. Do not defeat a lockout that was intentionally enabled for clinical reasons without staff approval. The Progressa provides caregiver lockout controls that can prevent selected bed-position functions from operating. Expected outcome: The section moves normally after the unintended lockout is removed. If movement is restored, confirm correct operation in both directions and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Test From Another Control Location
steps.instructions: Test the affected movement from each available control location, as applicable: Caregiver siderail control. Opposite caregiver siderail. Patient control. Graphical caregiver interface or footboard control. Compare the results. If the function works from one location but not another, the problem is likely isolated to a control panel, switch, cable, or local control connection. If the function fails from all locations, continue troubleshooting the power, frame, and actuator system. Expected outcome: Clinical Engineering determines whether the failure follows one control location or affects the complete articulation function. If only one control location is defective, label the affected control and evaluate whether the bed can safely remain in service under facility policy. Remove the bed from service when safe operation could be misunderstood or compromised.

steps.title: 5. Verify AC Power and Bed Power Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that the bed is connected to a known-good hospital-grade outlet. Check that the power cord is fully seated and undamaged. Inspect the plug and cord for cuts, crushing, exposed conductors, bent blades, discoloration, or heat damage. Verify that the outlet powers another approved test device or outlet tester. Confirm that the bed’s power indicators are illuminated normally. Reconnect AC power and allow the electrical system to stabilize before retesting. Do not use an extension cord or unapproved power strip. Expected outcome: The bed receives stable AC power and the articulation function operates normally. If all motorized functions are inoperative, suspect a general power, enable, control, or electrical-system problem rather than three simultaneous actuator failures.

steps.title: 6. Check for Battery-Only Behavior
steps.instructions: If the failure was reported during transport or while unplugged: Connect the bed to verified AC power. Allow sufficient time for a depleted battery system to begin recovering. Retest the affected section. Observe whether movement is slow, intermittent, or available only while connected to AC power. Expected outcome: Normal movement returns when adequate external power is supplied. If the bed works on AC but not on battery, document a battery-power complaint and route the bed for battery and charging-system evaluation.

steps.title: 7. Inspect for External Obstructions
steps.instructions: Examine the area around and beneath the affected frame section. Look for: Linens caught in the frame. Patient lift slings or straps. Tubing, cables, or drainage bags. Mattress retainers out of position. Equipment stored beneath the bed. Bedside furniture contacting the frame. Transport accessories interfering with movement. A wall, headwall, or other bed blocking articulation. Remove the obstruction only when it can be done safely. Expected outcome: The section travels freely without contacting external equipment or trapped materials. If removing the obstruction restores movement, inspect for damage before returning the bed to service.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Mattress and Surface Position
steps.instructions: Confirm that the mattress or therapeutic surface is installed and positioned correctly. Check that the surface is centered on the frame. Verify that mattress retainers are not bent, displaced, or trapping the surface. Look for excess linen buildup between articulating sections. Confirm that hoses, surface connections, and accessories have enough slack for normal articulation. Check whether the surface is folded, shifted, or binding at the head, knee, or foot section. Expected outcome: The surface follows the frame without resisting or obstructing articulation. Do not continue operating the bed if the surface or attached hoses are being stretched, pinched, or damaged.

steps.title: 9. Observe the Actuator Response
steps.instructions: Activate the affected control briefly and observe the response. Determine whether: The actuator is completely silent. A relay or control click is heard but no movement occurs. The motor runs but the frame does not move. The section moves slightly and stops. Grinding, popping, clicking, or binding is present. The frame twists or moves unevenly. An unusual smell or excessive heat is present. Do not repeatedly cycle a stalled actuator. Expected outcome: The observed behavior helps distinguish a control or power problem from mechanical binding, linkage failure, or an internal actuator fault. Immediately disconnect AC power and remove the bed from service if there is smoke, a burning odor, visible arcing, severe overheating, or unexpected frame movement.

steps.title: 10. Check Accessible Actuator and Cable Connections
steps.instructions: With the bed unplugged and removed from patient use, inspect only externally accessible connections. Look for a visibly loose actuator connector. Check for cables pulled tight, pinched, cut, crushed, or caught in the moving frame. Inspect connector housings for cracks, contamination, bent contacts, or incomplete engagement. Verify that accessible connectors are fully seated according to facility-approved procedures. Do not open the actuator, control module, junction box, or electrical enclosure. Expected outcome: Any obvious external connection problem is corrected without internal disassembly. If reseating an approved accessible connection restores operation, cycle the function through its normal range several times and complete all required safety and functional checks.

steps.title: 11. Inspect the Frame and Linkage Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect visible brackets, pivot points, pins, mounting hardware, and actuator attachment points. Look for: Bent or distorted frame components. Missing retaining clips or hardware. Loose actuator mounting points. Damaged welds. Linkage contacting another frame component. Evidence of impact or overload. Uneven movement between the left and right sides. Do not place any part of the body beneath an unsupported articulating section. Expected outcome: The bed frame and visible linkage appear intact and move without binding. A loose, bent, cracked, or disconnected structural component requires immediate removal from service.

steps.title: 12. Perform a Controlled Power Reset
steps.instructions: After ensuring that no patient is on the bed and no clinical therapy depends on it: Place the bed in a safe, stable condition. Disconnect the bed from AC power. Wait briefly for the control system to shut down. Reconnect the bed to a verified outlet. Allow the bed to complete its normal startup. Retest the affected movement from the caregiver controls. Do not perform repeated resets to keep an unreliable bed operational. Expected outcome: A temporary control-state problem clears and normal articulation returns. If movement returns, complete repeated functional testing before returning the bed to service.

steps.title: 13. Test the Complete Articulation System
steps.instructions: If the affected section begins operating, test: Head raise and lower. Knee raise and lower. Foot-related movement, when equipped. Bed height. Trendelenburg and reverse Trendelenburg. Automatic positioning functions, when applicable. Controls from each permitted location. Applicable lockouts. The Progressa uses coordinated powered positioning for several clinical configurations, so related movements should be checked for consistent operation. Expected outcome: All movements operate smoothly, consistently, and without abnormal noise, hesitation, binding, or unintended motion. Do not return the bed to service based on one successful button press.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the Hillrom Progressa head section would not raise or lower from either siderail control.
CCR.Cause: Verified AC power and lockout settings; found the head actuator remained silent from all controls with no external obstruction or visible cable damage.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the bed from service, labeled it Out of Service, and routed it for actuator and control-system bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Motor sound or relay click present
Grinding, binding, or uneven movement noted

title: Hillrom Progressa Hospital Bed - Chair Egress or Stand Assist Function Failure
description: Troubleshooting incomplete Chair Egress positioning or ineffective stand assistance caused by controls, brakes, footboard placement, obstructions, surface operation, or power issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot Chair Egress or Stand Assist movement while the bed is supporting an active patient. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Transfer the patient to another appropriate bed when continued care is required. Secure all patient lines, drainage devices, and accessories before moving the bed. Do not place anyone beneath or between moving frame sections. Use approved safe-patient-handling equipment when the patient cannot stand safely. Expected outcome: The patient is safely removed from dependence on a bed with unreliable positioning. If the bed moves unexpectedly, will not stop, or cannot safely support the patient, remove it from service immediately.

steps.title: 2. Clarify the Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The Chair control does not respond. The bed enters FullChair position but will not continue into Chair Egress. The bed will not lower completely. The foot section will not retract or lower. The seat or leg surface will not deflate. The bed does not tilt forward or lower the knee section. The back surface does not inflate for egress assistance. Movement stops and an audible tone or message appears. Record the complete displayed message, indicator behavior, and the last movement completed. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a specific portion of the Chair Egress sequence.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Bed Is Connected to Reliable AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The power cord is fully connected. The outlet is operational and appropriate for medical equipment. The power cord and plug have no visible damage. The bed indicates that external power is present. Test the outlet with an approved receptacle tester or another verified device according to facility policy. Chair Egress requires several powered frame and surface movements. A weak battery or missing AC supply may prevent the sequence from completing. Expected outcome: The bed operates from stable external power. If restoring AC power resolves the issue, complete a functional test and stop.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Brakes Are Set
steps.instructions: Engage the bed brakes fully and verify that the brake indicator shows the expected condition. The Progressa operating instructions require the brakes to be set before Chair Egress is activated. Attempt the function again without a patient. Expected outcome: The bed recognizes the brake condition and permits the Chair Egress sequence. If setting the brakes resolves the issue, verify repeatable operation and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Footboard and Foot-End Area
steps.instructions: Remove the footboard before completing Chair Egress. Store it securely and do not leave it flat where it could become contaminated or create a trip hazard. Inspect for: A footboard still installed after the bed reaches FullChair. Equipment attached to the footboard. Linens caught in the retracting foot section. Cables, hoses, drainage bags, or accessories obstructing movement. Furniture or equipment blocking the foot end of the bed. With the footboard installed, the bed may stop at FullChair and provide a tone rather than continuing into the full egress position. Expected outcome: The foot section has adequate clearance to retract and lower. If removing the obstruction resolves the issue, inspect for damage, complete the movement test, and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check the Controls and Lockout Settings
steps.instructions: Inspect the Chair control on the caregiver siderail and any connected caregiver pendant. Confirm that: The button is not physically damaged, stuck, or contaminated. The siderail is securely positioned. No articulation or control lockout is preventing operation. Other caregiver frame controls respond normally. The pendant connector, when equipped, is fully seated and undamaged. Test the Chair control from another available caregiver control location. Expected outcome: At least one caregiver control initiates and sustains the Chair sequence. If one control works and another does not, the issue is likely isolated to the affected siderail control, pendant, cable, or connection. Remove the bed from service for repair.

steps.title: 7. Use the Correct Control Sequence
steps.instructions: With the bed empty, brakes set, footboard removed, and the area clear: Press and continuously hold the Chair control. Allow the bed to move through the FullChair sequence. Continue following any on-screen instructions. After the surface-deflation indication or three-tone signal, continue holding or press and hold the Chair control as directed. Confirm that the bed lowers, tilts, retracts the foot section, and lowers the knee section. Hold the Chair control again when testing the optional back-inflation egress assistance. The control must generally remain held during movement. Releasing it may stop the sequence as a safety feature. Expected outcome: The complete Chair Egress sequence operates without interruption. If correct control operation resolves the complaint, return the bed to a flat position, repeat the test, and stop.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Mattress Surface and Connections
steps.instructions: If the frame moves but the seat, leg, or back sections do not inflate or deflate correctly: Confirm the installed surface is compatible with the bed configuration. Inspect visible surface hoses and connectors for disconnection, kinking, pinching, or damage. Confirm the mattress is centered and properly seated on the frame. Check for linens or accessories compressing the surface hoses. Listen for the surface blower or compressor during the commanded movement. Note any surface-related messages or alarms. On equipped Progressa beds, Chair Egress includes deflation of the seat and leg sections, with optional back-section inflation for egress assistance. Expected outcome: The surface responds correctly during the positioning sequence. If reseating an accessible external connection resolves the issue, repeat the complete function test and stop.

steps.title: 9. Check for Mechanical Obstruction or Uneven Movement
steps.instructions: Observe the empty bed while commanding Chair Egress. Look and listen for: One frame section moving while another remains stationary. Binding, jerking, or uneven movement. Grinding, clicking, or repeated actuator noise. Damaged or bent foot-section components. Objects trapped in the frame. A section reaching its travel limit before the sequence is complete. Movement that stops consistently at the same position. Do not force any frame section or manually push the bed through the sequence. Expected outcome: All frame sections move smoothly, evenly, and without unusual noise. If movement is uneven, mechanically restricted, or accompanied by unusual noise, stop testing and remove the bed from service.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Power Reset
steps.instructions: Only after the bed is empty and clinically released: Return the bed to a stable position when possible. Disconnect the bed from AC power. Follow facility-approved procedures to place the bed in a fully powered-down state. Wait briefly. Reconnect the bed to a verified AC outlet. Allow the system to initialize completely. Retest Chair Egress without a patient. Do not repeatedly reset a bed that displays persistent errors or moves unpredictably. Expected outcome: Temporary control or communication faults clear and normal operation returns. If the function works after the reset, repeat the test several times and verify all related controls before returning the bed to service.

steps.title: 11. Complete a Final Functional and Safety Check
steps.instructions: Before returning the bed to clinical use, verify: Brakes and steering operate correctly. Bed height adjustment functions normally. Head, knee, and foot sections move smoothly. FullChair and Chair Egress complete without interruption. Surface inflation and deflation operate as equipped. Both available caregiver controls function correctly. The bed returns safely to the flat position. No error messages, unusual sounds, or unintended movements occur. Power cord, siderails, footboard, and accessories are secure. Expected outcome: The bed repeatedly completes the intended positioning sequence and is safe for clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Hillrom Progressa entered FullChair position but would not continue into Chair Egress or inflate the back section for stand assistance.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the footboard remained installed and linens were obstructing the retracting foot section, preventing completion of the Chair Egress sequence.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the footboard and obstruction, verified brakes and AC power, and successfully tested FullChair, Chair Egress, surface deflation, back inflation, and return-to-flat operation.

helpfulDetails: Exact error message or tone sequence
Unusual sounds, binding, or uneven movement

title: Hillrom Progressa Hospital Bed - Turn Assist or Continuous Lateral Rotation Failure
description: Troubleshooting unavailable, incomplete, uneven, or interrupted Turn Assist and Continuous Lateral Rotation caused by positioning, controls, surface setup, or external obstruction.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot rotation or Turn Assist while the feature is moving an unattended patient. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Stop the active therapy using the touchscreen controls. Return the surface to Normal mode. Reposition or transfer the patient when the bed cannot safely support the ordered therapy. Secure all IV lines, drains, ventilator tubing, monitoring cables, and other attachments before testing. Expected outcome: The patient is stable, appropriately supported, and no lines or equipment are at risk of being pulled or compressed. If the bed moves unexpectedly, rotates excessively, or cannot be stopped normally, remove it from service immediately.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: Turn Assist does not appear on the touchscreen. Left Turn Assist works but Right Turn Assist does not, or vice versa. The surface begins to turn but stops early. Continuous Lateral Rotation Therapy does not start. Rotation stops after another pulmonary therapy is changed. The touchscreen displays an error, advisory, or therapy restriction. The surface inflates but does not rotate the patient. Record the complete message and the selected therapy settings. Expected outcome: The reported problem is clearly separated into a control, setup, pneumatic, or movement issue.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Installed Surface Supports the Requested Feature
steps.instructions: Confirm the Progressa is equipped with the powered therapeutic surface required for Turn Assist or Continuous Lateral Rotation. Inspect for: The correct integrated air surface. A recognized surface displayed on the caregiver interface. Available Surface and Pulmonary Therapy menus. Missing or disabled rotation controls. Continuous Lateral Rotation is an optional therapy associated with compatible pulmonary or therapy surfaces and may not be available on every Progressa configuration. Expected outcome: The installed bed and surface configuration supports the requested therapy. If the feature is not included with the installed surface, stop troubleshooting and explain the configuration limitation.

steps.title: 4. Check AC Power and Bed Status
steps.instructions: Verify that: The bed is connected directly to a known-good hospital-grade outlet. The AC power indicator is illuminated. The power cord and plug are undamaged. The bed is not relying solely on battery power. No power-related messages are displayed. Test the outlet with an approved tester or another verified device when needed. Expected outcome: Stable AC power is available for the bed frame, air system, and therapy functions. If restoring power resolves the issue, verify normal operation and stop.

steps.title: 5. Confirm the Bed Is Braked and Properly Positioned
steps.instructions: Set the brake and place the bed in a safe, stable position. Check that: All casters are stationary. The bed is not contacting a wall, boom, bedside cabinet, lift, or other equipment. The frame and siderails have adequate clearance. The head, knee, and foot sections are not in an unusual position that could restrict therapy. The patient is centered on the surface. Expected outcome: Nothing external prevents safe inflation or side-to-side movement. If removing an obstruction resolves the issue, verify the complete therapy cycle and stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Surface and External Connections
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the mattress and accessible connections without opening the bed or surface. Look for: A disconnected or partially seated surface connector. Pinched, kinked, twisted, or trapped hoses. Hoses caught between the mattress, frame, siderail, or foot section. A visibly deflated surface section. Tears, punctures, fluid intrusion, or damaged covers. Unusual air leakage or continuous compressor operation. Reseat only user-accessible connectors according to facility procedures. Expected outcome: The surface is properly connected, intact, and able to inflate without restriction. If a damaged surface or hose is found, remove the bed from service and arrange repair.

steps.title: 7. Verify Siderail Position for Turn Assist
steps.instructions: Raise the siderails required for safe operation before initiating Turn Assist. The Progressa control guidance states that the siderails must be raised to activate Turn Assist. Once the turn begins, a siderail may be lowered for care, but the bed will alarm as a safety precaution. Then: Select the Surface menu. Confirm the surface is in Normal mode. Select Left Turn Assist or Right Turn Assist. Observe whether the appropriate side inflates and supports the turn. Expected outcome: The selected Turn Assist function inflates the correct side of the surface. If raising the siderails restores operation, verify both directions and stop.

steps.title: 8. Check for Control Locks or Disabled Functions
steps.instructions: Inspect the caregiver controls for lockout indicators. Verify that: Surface controls are not locked. Pulmonary therapy controls are available. The caregiver touchscreen responds to selections. The selected command highlights or acknowledges input. No control-lock indicator remains active. Unlock controls only according to facility policy. Expected outcome: The caregiver can select and activate the required surface therapy. If removing a control lock resolves the issue, test the feature and stop.

steps.title: 9. Return the Surface to Normal Mode
steps.instructions: From the caregiver touchscreen: Select Surface. Select Normal. Allow the surface to stabilize. Retry Turn Assist. Turn Assist is deactivated by returning the surface to Normal mode. Also verify that the surface is not left in: Max-Inflate. Sleep Mode. Seat Deflate. Opti-Rest. Patient Comfort adjustment. Expected outcome: The surface exits conflicting modes and accepts a new Turn Assist command. If Normal mode restores operation, complete a functional test and stop.

steps.title: 10. Re-enter Continuous Lateral Rotation Settings
steps.instructions: For Continuous Lateral Rotation: Select Pulmonary Therapy on the caregiver interface. Select Rotation. Review the left and right turn angles, pause time, and therapy duration. Confirm the settings are accepted. Start the therapy and observe the initial cycle. The bed’s pulmonary therapy screen provides access to Rotation and other therapy functions. Expected outcome: The bed begins the programmed rotation sequence and alternates sides as configured. If correcting the settings resolves the issue, verify several direction changes and stop.

steps.title: 11. Check Whether Another Therapy Stopped Rotation
steps.instructions: Determine whether Percussion and Vibration therapy was recently running. On the Progressa, stopping Percussion and Vibration while both therapies are active can also stop Continuous Lateral Rotation. Rotation must then be manually reactivated. Return to the Pulmonary Therapy menu and restart Rotation. Expected outcome: Continuous Lateral Rotation resumes after being reactivated. If the therapy now operates normally, stop.

steps.title: 12. Remove Excess Bedding or Positioning Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect for items that could prevent the surface from changing shape: Excess sheets or blankets tucked tightly under the mattress. Positioning wedges or rigid supports. Patient lifts, transfer sheets, or straps caught beneath the patient. Equipment resting against the mattress sides. Tubing or cables trapped between the surface and frame. Remove or reposition items only with clinical staff present. Expected outcome: The surface can inflate and rotate freely without external resistance. If correcting the obstruction resolves the problem, verify therapy operation and stop.

steps.title: 13. Perform an Unoccupied Functional Test
steps.instructions: After the patient has been safely transferred: Confirm AC power and brakes. Leave the surface installed normally. Raise the required siderails. Select Normal mode. Test Left Turn Assist. Return to Normal. Test Right Turn Assist. Start a low or facility-approved Continuous Lateral Rotation setting. Observe inflation, direction changes, alarms, and displayed errors. Listen for: Compressor operation. Repeated air venting. Clicking without inflation. Uneven inflation. Abnormal mechanical or pneumatic sounds. Expected outcome: Both Turn Assist directions and rotation operate consistently without errors, leaks, or unexpected stopping. Do not return the bed to service when the failure cannot be reproduced reliably or the therapy remains intermittent.

steps.title: 14. Power-Cycle the Bed When Clinically Safe
steps.instructions: With the bed unoccupied: Stop all therapies. Return the surface to Normal. Disconnect AC power. Allow the system to shut down according to facility procedures. Reconnect it to a verified outlet. Allow the touchscreen and surface system to initialize fully. Repeat the functional test. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a bed that displays a persistent error code. Expected outcome: The surface controller initializes normally and therapy controls return. If the feature operates normally after restart, document the event and complete an extended operational test before returning the bed to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Progressa bed would inflate in Normal mode but would not start Right Turn Assist or Continuous Lateral Rotation.
CCR.Cause: Right-side therapy remained unavailable after confirming AC power, raised siderails, Normal surface mode, clear hoses, correct settings, and an unobstructed mattress.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the bed from service, applied an Out of Service label, documented the failed unoccupied therapy test, and sent the bed for surface and pneumatic-system evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Left and Right Turn Assist results

title: Hillrom Progressa Hospital Bed - Surface Pressure Zone or Therapy Mode Fault
description: Troubleshooting pressure-zone, inflation, Max-Inflate, rotation, percussion, vibration, or other surface therapy faults caused by setup, connections, positioning, or surface problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable surface or therapy function while it is supporting an active patient. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Transfer the patient to another appropriate bed or support surface when pressure redistribution or pulmonary therapy is required. Follow facility procedures for protecting the patient during transfer. Do not leave a high-risk patient on a surface with visibly deflated or uneven pressure zones. Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported without relying on the affected surface. If the surface cannot maintain appropriate inflation, remove the bed from clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Fault
steps.instructions: Record the complete message displayed on the Graphical Caregiver Interface and determine whether the complaint involves: One pressure zone appearing soft or deflated. The entire surface failing to inflate. Max-Inflate failing to activate or remain active. Continuous lateral rotation therapy not starting. Percussion or vibration therapy not starting. A therapy stopping unexpectedly. A surface mode being unavailable or grayed out. Repeated surface or therapy fault messages. The Progressa may be equipped with prevention, pulmonary, or therapy surface configurations, so available functions can vary by bed. Expected outcome: The affected function and surface configuration are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Check AC Power and Bed Status
steps.instructions: Verify that: The power cord is fully connected to the bed. The cord is connected directly to a verified hospital-grade outlet. The bed indicates that external AC power is present. The outlet operates correctly when tested with an approved device or receptacle tester. The bed is not relying solely on battery power during therapy testing. Surface inflation and powered therapy functions require reliable electrical power. Expected outcome: The bed remains powered without interruptions or power-related messages. If restoring AC power resolves the fault, perform a functional check and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Allow the Surface to Complete Initialization
steps.instructions: If the bed was recently powered on, transported, disconnected, or placed into CPR deflation: Confirm the CPR release is fully reset. Allow the surface time to reinflate and stabilize. Do not repeatedly select different therapy modes during initialization. Observe whether the displayed pressure-zone indicators return to normal. Expected outcome: All surface zones inflate evenly and the selected surface mode becomes available. If the surface initializes normally and maintains pressure, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Surface Externally
steps.instructions: Remove linens only as necessary and inspect for: A surface that is folded, bunched, shifted, or incorrectly positioned. Linens, transfer devices, or accessories compressing the surface. Visible cuts, punctures, tears, abrasion, or fluid intrusion. A section that remains noticeably softer than adjacent sections. Patient-positioning equipment interfering with inflation. An incorrect or incompatible surface installed on the bed. Do not probe punctures, patch the surface, or open the surface assembly unless specifically authorized by Hillrom service documentation. Expected outcome: The surface is correctly positioned, unobstructed, and free of visible damage. If visible damage is found, remove the bed from service and arrange surface replacement or repair.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Accessible Surface Connections
steps.instructions: With the patient removed and the bed safely powered down when appropriate: Locate the externally accessible surface hose and connector area. Verify each connector is fully seated and locked. Check for pinched, sharply bent, stretched, twisted, or disconnected hoses. Inspect connectors for contamination, damaged seals, bent fittings, or broken retaining features. Confirm the surface connection has not loosened during transport or cleaning. Do not remove covers or access internal pneumatic components. Expected outcome: All accessible pneumatic connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an accessible connection resolves the fault, restart the bed and complete a functional test.

steps.title: 7. Confirm Bed and Surface Positioning
steps.instructions: Place the bed in a safe, neutral position and verify: The frame is not against a wall or equipment. The surface is aligned with the frame. The foot section is adjusted appropriately. The siderails and frame sections are not trapping the surface or hoses. No equipment is resting on or pulling against the mattress assembly. Some therapy functions may be restricted by bed position, patient position, surface configuration, or an active safety condition. Expected outcome: The bed permits the requested surface or therapy function without a positioning-related message.

steps.title: 8. Verify Patient Weight Information
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The patient’s weight is within the bed and installed surface limits. The scale has been zeroed according to facility practice when appropriate. The displayed weight is reasonable. Excess equipment has not been added after the bed was zeroed. The surface is not attempting to regulate around an obviously incorrect weight value. The Progressa surface uses bed and patient information to support pressure redistribution and therapy operation. Expected outcome: The displayed weight is plausible and the surface pressure zones stabilize. If correcting the weight setup resolves the issue, test the surface again and stop.

steps.title: 9. Test a Basic Surface Function
steps.instructions: With no patient on the bed, or with an approved test load when required by facility procedures: Select the standard pressure-redistribution mode. Observe whether all zones inflate. Activate Max-Inflate if available. Confirm that the surface becomes uniformly firm. Cancel Max-Inflate and verify that the surface returns to its normal operating mode. Listen for continuous air leakage, repeated valve cycling, or abnormal compressor noise. Expected outcome: The surface changes modes, inflates evenly, and maintains pressure without a fault. If a specific zone remains deflated or the pump runs continuously, suspect a leak, valve problem, sensor problem, or internal pneumatic failure.

steps.title: 10. Test the Reported Therapy Mode
steps.instructions: Only when safe and when the installed surface supports the function: Select the reported therapy mode. Confirm all required settings are entered. Verify that no incompatible bed position or mode is active. Start the therapy and observe the display. Confirm the therapy begins and progresses through the expected sequence. Stop the therapy using the normal control. Progressa configurations may support continuous lateral rotation therapy and, on applicable surfaces, percussion and vibration therapy. Expected outcome: The therapy starts, operates, and stops without a fault. If the therapy repeatedly stops or faults under correct conditions, discontinue testing and escalate.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After the patient has been removed and clinical staff have approved: Record the fault message before restarting. Turn the bed off using the normal procedure. Disconnect AC power briefly according to facility policy. Reconnect the bed to verified AC power. Allow the bed and surface to initialize completely. Retest the standard surface mode before testing advanced therapies. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a bed that continues to display the same fault. Expected outcome: The surface completes initialization and operates normally. If the fault returns, treat it as a persistent failure.

steps.title: 12. Verify Operation Before Returning the Bed to Service
steps.instructions: Before releasing the bed: Confirm all surface zones remain inflated. Verify the standard pressure-redistribution mode. Verify Max-Inflate, if equipped. Test the originally reported therapy function. Confirm there are no active surface fault messages. Inspect for unusual sounds, heat, odor, or continuous air leakage. Allow the bed to operate long enough to confirm the fault does not immediately return. Expected outcome: The surface maintains pressure and all applicable therapy functions operate reliably.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Progressa displayed a surface pressure-zone fault and would not start continuous lateral rotation therapy.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the accessible surface air connector partially disengaged, preventing the surface from maintaining pressure in the affected zone.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the bed from patient use, reseated and secured the surface connector, restarted the bed, and verified normal inflation, Max-Inflate, and rotation therapy operation.

helpfulDetails: Uneven or deflated pressure zone identified
Air leakage or unusual compressor noise

title: Hillrom Progressa Hospital Bed - Touchscreen, Caregiver Controls, or Pendant Unresponsive
description: Troubleshooting unresponsive touchscreen, siderail caregiver controls, or pendant functions caused by power, lockouts, connections, contamination, or external control damage.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot bed positioning controls while the bed is supporting an unstable, unattended, or actively treated patient. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Transfer the patient to another verified bed when positioning, therapy, or emergency functions cannot be reliably operated. Confirm the brakes are engaged. Keep the bed in its lowest safe position whenever possible. Ensure lines, drains, tubes, and other equipment will not be pulled if the bed moves unexpectedly. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from unintended bed movement, loss of positioning, or delayed access to required functions. If essential positioning or emergency controls cannot be operated safely, remove the bed from clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Clarify Which Controls Are Unresponsive
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects: The Graphic Caregiver Interface touchscreen; one caregiver siderail control panel; both caregiver siderail control panels; the patient pendant; patient-side controls only; a single function, such as head, knee, height, chair, or Trendelenburg; or all bed articulation and touchscreen functions. Test only when the bed is unoccupied or when clinical staff confirm testing is safe. Expected outcome: The affected control area and failure pattern are clearly identified. A single failed control station suggests a localized control or connection problem. Multiple unresponsive control locations may indicate lockout, power, software, or internal communication failure.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Bed Has Electrical Power
steps.instructions: Verify that the power cord is fully inserted into a known-good hospital-grade outlet, the outlet is energized, the power cord and plug show no cuts, bent blades, looseness, or heat damage, the bed’s power indicators illuminate, and the bed responds when connected to another verified outlet. Do not use an extension cord or unapproved power strip. Expected outcome: The bed powers normally from a verified AC source. If operation returns after correcting the outlet or power connection, confirm all controls function normally and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Allow the Bed to Recharge
steps.instructions: If the bed was unplugged for an extended period, connect it to AC power and allow the battery system to charge. Observe whether the touchscreen becomes active, control indicators illuminate, bed functions respond while connected to AC power, and battery or low-power warnings clear. A severely discharged battery may prevent normal operation when the bed is unplugged. Expected outcome: Controls operate normally while the bed is connected to AC power. If controls work on AC power but fail immediately when unplugged, remove the bed from service for battery evaluation.

steps.title: 5. Check for Activated Control Lockouts
steps.instructions: Inspect the caregiver control panel and touchscreen for illuminated lockout indicators. Verify whether articulation functions have been intentionally locked out, including head movement, knee movement, bed height, patient controls, and other configured functions. The Progressa caregiver controls include lockout functions that can disable selected articulation controls. Release only those lockouts that clinical staff confirm should be enabled. Expected outcome: Previously locked functions respond normally after the appropriate lockout is released. If releasing the lockout restores operation, verify the control from each applicable location and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Confirm the Screen Is Not Displaying a Blocking Message
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen for warning messages, help screens, confirmation prompts, service indicators, active therapy screens, a screen that is illuminated but frozen, or an unusually dim display. Acknowledge only messages that can be safely cleared without changing prescribed patient therapy or clinical settings. Record the exact wording of any persistent message. Expected outcome: The normal caregiver interface is displayed and accepts input.

steps.title: 7. Clean and Dry the Control Surfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen, siderail controls, and pendant for moisture, cleaning solution residue, gel or lotion, adhesive residue, linens pressing against buttons, dirt around control edges, and physical objects contacting the touchscreen. Clean the external surfaces using facility-approved methods, then dry them completely. Do not spray liquid directly into control panels, connectors, or seams. Expected outcome: Controls respond normally after external contamination or unintended contact is removed. If cleaning resolves the issue, test each affected control several times and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Pendant and External Cable
steps.instructions: If the pendant is affected, examine the pendant housing for cracks, fluid intrusion, or impact damage; inspect the cable for cuts, crushing, stretching, or sharp bends; check the connector for looseness or visible damage; confirm the cable is not trapped beneath the bed frame, siderail, caster, or mattress; and reseat only user-accessible connectors permitted by facility procedure. Do not open the pendant housing or disassemble the connector. Expected outcome: The pendant is securely connected and functions without intermittent response. If a known-compatible, facility-approved pendant is available, substitution may help distinguish a pendant failure from a bed-side control problem.

steps.title: 9. Inspect the Siderails and Control Panels
steps.instructions: Check each siderail for full mechanical engagement, impact damage, loose or cracked control overlays, buttons that remain physically depressed, evidence of fluid entry, pinched or exposed wiring, and failure limited to a siderail that was recently raised, lowered, or struck. Raise and lower the siderail only when safe, then confirm it locks securely. Expected outcome: The siderail is mechanically secure and its controls operate normally. A control panel that works intermittently as the siderail moves should be considered unreliable. Remove the bed from service.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Power Reset
steps.instructions: Only perform a reset when the bed is unoccupied or the patient has been safely transferred. Place the bed in a stable, low position if controls permit. Disconnect the AC power cord. Allow the bed to remain disconnected briefly according to facility procedure. Reconnect the bed directly to a verified outlet. Allow the system to complete its startup process. Do not repeatedly press controls during startup. Expected outcome: The touchscreen initializes and the caregiver controls respond normally. If operation returns, complete a full functional check before returning the bed to service. A recurring freeze or need for repeated resets requires bench evaluation.

steps.title: 11. Test Each Control Location Separately
steps.instructions: After power and lockouts are verified, test left caregiver siderail controls, right caregiver siderail controls, touchscreen functions, pendant controls, patient controls when applicable, and head, knee, height, and other basic articulation functions. The Progressa provides caregiver siderail controls for functions such as head and knee positioning, with position information also available through the caregiver interface. Expected outcome: Each control produces the intended movement without delay, sticking, or intermittent operation. Stop immediately if movement is unexpected, reversed, intermittent, or continues after the control is released.

steps.title: 12. Check for Evidence of Internal Failure
steps.instructions: Remove the bed from service if the touchscreen stays blank despite verified AC power, the screen freezes repeatedly, multiple control stations remain unresponsive, controls work intermittently, bed movement occurs without a command, a function continues after the button is released, a control panel shows liquid damage, a persistent service code or communication error appears, or there is unusual heat, odor, sound, or visible damage. Do not open the touchscreen, siderails, control modules, or electrical enclosures unless trained and authorized under the manufacturer’s service procedures. Hillrom provides dedicated technical training and service documentation for Progressa maintenance and diagnostic work beyond basic external troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Progressa touchscreen and right caregiver siderail controls did not respond to commands.
CCR.Cause: Verified AC power and control lockouts; the right siderail control panel remained unresponsive and showed evidence of intermittent operation when the siderail moved.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the bed from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for bench evaluation of the siderail control and communication system.

helpfulDetails: Bed connected to a verified outlet
Left and right caregiver controls tested
Siderails checked for damage and secure engagement
Unusual sound, heat, odor, or fluid intrusion noted

title: Hillrom Progressa Hospital Bed - Network, Wi-Fi, or Bed Status Communication Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing network connectivity, failed bed-status reporting, intermittent communication, or absent data caused by power, location, configuration, or external network issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions:
Do not interrupt essential bed functions, reposition the bed, or perform troubleshooting that could affect patient support while the bed is occupied.

Notify the responsible clinical staff.
Confirm the patient is safely positioned.
Maintain required bed-exit, siderail, brake, and low-position precautions.
Transfer the patient to another verified bed if the communication problem affects a required safety workflow.
Do not assume central monitoring or remote bed-status displays accurately reflect the bed’s current condition during a communication failure.

Expected outcome: The patient remains safely supported without dependence on inaccurate or unavailable network information.

If the bed’s local controls, alarms, or therapeutic functions are also malfunctioning, remove it from clinical use and evaluate it separately.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions:
Determine what information is not communicating:

The bed does not appear on the facility network.
The bed appears offline in the monitoring or asset-management application.
Bed-exit, brake, siderail, head-angle, or low-bed status is not updating.
The displayed room or bed assignment is incorrect.
Communication is intermittent.
The bed communicates in one room but not another.
The problem began after the bed was moved, serviced, replaced, or reassigned.

Record any displayed network symbol, communication message, error code, or central-system alert.

Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the bed, its location, a specific data type, or the receiving system.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Bed’s Local Operation
steps.instructions:
Test the bed’s basic functions from its local controls:

Power indicators operate normally.
Bed positioning responds correctly.
Brake and siderail indicators reflect the actual bed condition.
Bed-exit functions operate locally when tested according to facility policy.
The touchscreen or caregiver controls are responsive.
No unrelated system errors are displayed.

The Progressa is a smart ICU bed platform, but network communication should be evaluated separately from its essential local bed functions.

Expected outcome: Local operation is normal, confirming that the reported issue is primarily related to communication.

If local status indicators are also incorrect, stop and escalate for bed control or sensor evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Confirm AC Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions:
Verify that:

The power cord is fully inserted into the bed.
The plug is secure in a known-good hospital-grade outlet.
The outlet has power.
The bed indicates that it is operating from AC power.
No damaged plug, cord, strain relief, or unusual heat is present.
The battery is not fully depleted.

If permitted, disconnect and reconnect the AC plug after confirming the patient will remain safe.

Some network components may require the bed to be powered and fully operational before communication resumes.

Expected outcome: The bed has stable power and any temporary power-related communication interruption clears.

If communication returns, verify correct reporting at the receiving system and stop.

steps.title: 5. Allow Time for Reconnection After Power-Up or Movement
steps.instructions:
If the bed was recently:

Powered on
Unplugged
Transported
Moved between units
Returned from repair
Assigned to a new room

Allow the approved connection period for the bed to rejoin the wireless network and update the receiving application.

Do not repeatedly power-cycle the bed, as this may restart the connection process.

Expected outcome: The bed reconnects and its current location and status populate correctly.

steps.title: 6. Check the Bed’s Physical Location
steps.instructions:
Determine whether the failure occurs:

In one patient room only
Near elevators, imaging equipment, utility spaces, or shielded walls
At the edge of a wireless coverage area
Only while the bed is in a hallway or transport route
After relocation to another floor or building area

Move the unoccupied bed, or safely test it during a controlled service evaluation, in a location where another Progressa bed is known to communicate.

Expected outcome: Communication behavior helps distinguish a bed-specific problem from a wireless coverage or infrastructure problem.

If multiple beds fail in the same area, escalate to the network or clinical systems team rather than replacing bed components.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Bed
steps.instructions:
Check whether another appropriately configured Progressa bed communicates from the same room or network area.

If neither bed communicates, suspect wireless coverage, access-point, server, interface, or receiving-system problems.
If the known-good bed communicates normally, continue troubleshooting the affected bed.
Do not move an occupied bed solely for testing unless the move is clinically approved.

Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to either the individual bed or the facility infrastructure.

steps.title: 8. Verify Bed Identity and Assignment
steps.instructions:
Confirm that the identifiers used by the connected system match the physical bed:

Asset number
Serial number
Network or device identifier
Room and bed assignment
Facility or unit assignment
Hostname or equipment record, if visible to Clinical Engineering

Look for duplicate records, retired-device entries, incorrect room assignments, or a recently replaced communication module.

Expected outcome: The physical bed is correctly associated with its network and application record.

If correcting the assignment restores communication, verify several status changes and stop.

steps.title: 9. Inspect Accessible Communication Components
steps.instructions:
Without opening covers or performing internal disassembly, inspect accessible areas for:

Loose or damaged external communication accessories
Missing covers or antennas, when externally visible
Evidence of liquid intrusion
Impact damage near the head-end electronics
Pinched cables
Damaged connectors
Signs that an accessory was removed during cleaning or repair

Do not probe internal connectors or remove electronic assemblies unless authorized by the applicable service procedure.

Expected outcome: No visible external damage or disconnected accessory is present.

If damage is found, remove the bed from service and arrange repair.

steps.title: 10. Review Available Network Indicators
steps.instructions:
If the installed configuration provides network or connection indicators, record:

Connected, disconnected, or searching status
Wireless signal indication
Communication error messages
Last-connected time
Software or configuration warnings
Whether the identifier shown matches the bed

Do not change protected network settings without approved values and coordination with the responsible network team.

Expected outcome: The displayed state identifies whether the bed is failing to join the network or whether data is failing farther downstream.

steps.title: 11. Confirm the Receiving System Is Operational
steps.instructions:
Check the appropriate central application, middleware, nurse-call interface, remote-management platform, or bed-status dashboard.

Determine whether:

Other beds are updating normally.
The affected bed is shown as offline.
Data is delayed rather than completely absent.
Only one type of status is missing.
The server or interface is under maintenance.
A facility-wide outage has been reported.

Hillrom offers connected-device and remote-management capabilities for supported bed configurations, so a communication problem may involve systems outside the bed itself.

Expected outcome: The receiving system is verified as available, or the issue is referred to the team responsible for that system.

steps.title: 12. Coordinate With the Network or Clinical Systems Team
steps.instructions:
Provide the responsible team with:

Bed asset and serial numbers
Device or network identifier
Current room
Time the failure was observed
Whether the bed ever connects
Results from a known-good-room test
Whether other beds are affected
Relevant screenshots or error messages

Request confirmation that the bed is:

Authorized on the wireless network
Associated with an access point
Receiving the correct network configuration
Reaching the required server or interface
Properly enrolled in the applicable management system

Expected outcome: Infrastructure, enrollment, and application-side causes are either corrected or ruled out.

steps.title: 13. Perform an Approved Restart When Safe
steps.instructions:
Only after confirming patient safety and facility policy:

Remove the bed from patient use, if necessary.
Record current settings and displayed errors.
Perform the manufacturer-approved shutdown or restart process.
Restore AC power.
Allow the bed to complete initialization.
Recheck network and central-system status.

Do not repeatedly cycle power or disconnect internal batteries as a troubleshooting shortcut.

Expected outcome: A temporary software or connection state clears and normal communication returns.

If communication returns, verify multiple bed-status changes before returning the bed to service.

steps.title: 14. Verify Communication With a Functional Test
steps.instructions:
Before closing the work order, confirm that the receiving system correctly reports several safe, controlled status changes, as supported by the installed configuration:

Brake applied or released
Bed raised or lowered
Siderail position
Head-of-bed angle
Bed-exit monitoring state
Room or bed assignment

Return each feature to the clinically appropriate condition after testing.

Expected outcome: Local bed status and remote system status agree without unusual delay.

If all tested data updates correctly, return the bed to service and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Hillrom Progressa bed appeared offline and its brake, siderail, and bed-exit status were not updating at the central display.
CCR.Cause: Bed functions operated normally, but the device failed to communicate in multiple known-good wireless locations while other Progressa beds remained online.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the bed from service, labeled it Out of Service, documented its network identifier and error behavior, and sent it for communication-module evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Network or clinical systems team contacted
Visible damage or liquid intrusion noted

title: Hillrom VersaCare Hospital Bed - Battery Not Charging Or Bed Loses Functions On Backup Power
description: Troubleshooting charging problems, short battery operation, lost bed functions, power-source issues, damaged cords, connections, controls, or an aged battery.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unreliable backup power while a patient depends on the bed for positioning, alarms, transport, or emergency functions. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Connect the bed to a verified AC source when safe. Transfer the patient to another verified bed if dependable powered operation cannot be maintained. Keep the bed brakes set and the bed in a safe position. Do not transport the patient relying on an unverified battery. Expected outcome: The patient remains supported by a bed with dependable power and positioning functions. If reliable operation cannot be maintained, remove the bed from clinical use and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the bed: Does not indicate charging while connected to AC power. Operates normally on AC but loses all functions when unplugged. Operates on battery briefly and then stops. Loses only selected functions on battery. Displays a battery, power, or service indication. Has been stored unplugged or recently returned from transport. Record the condition before cycling power or reconnecting accessories. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as a charging, battery-runtime, power-input, or function-specific problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Power Cord and Plug
steps.instructions: Disconnect the bed from AC power and inspect the accessible power cord, plug, strain relief, and cord storage area. Look for: Cuts, crushing, exposed conductors, or melted insulation. Bent, loose, burned, or contaminated plug blades. Damage where the cord enters the bed. A cord that has been pulled tightly, rolled over, or pinched by the frame. Evidence of fluid intrusion, overheating, or an unusual odor. Do not continue using a damaged power cord. Expected outcome: The power cord and plug are intact, clean, securely attached, and safe to energize. If damage is found, remove the bed from service and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Connect the bed directly to a known-good hospital-grade receptacle. Avoid extension cords and unverified power strips. Confirm the receptacle supports another suitable test device or is verified with approved electrical test equipment. Confirm that the plug remains fully seated. Observe whether AC power and charging indications respond normally. Expected outcome: The bed recognizes a verified AC source and begins normal charging behavior. If the bed charges normally from the known-good outlet, correct or report the original receptacle or infrastructure problem. Troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Allow Adequate Charging Opportunity
steps.instructions: If the bed has been stored unplugged, recently transported, or deeply discharged: Leave it connected to a verified AC source. Confirm that the bed remains plugged in continuously during evaluation. Observe whether the battery or charging indication changes over time. Do not judge battery condition from only a brief connection to AC power. Do not invent or assume a charging time. Follow current Hillrom documentation when a specified charge period is required. Expected outcome: Charging indications remain stable and available battery operation improves after an appropriate charging period. If normal battery operation returns and all required functions pass testing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Accessible Power and Battery Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect any externally accessible power switches, battery-enable controls, or removable battery connections provided for normal service access. Confirm switches are in the required operating position. Verify that accessible connectors are fully seated. Look for looseness, corrosion, contamination, bent contacts, or damaged retaining features. Do not open sealed battery assemblies or bypass protective circuits. Do not access internal boards or perform deep disassembly. Expected outcome: All accessible power and battery controls are correctly positioned, and external connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an approved accessible connection restores charging, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare AC and Battery Operation
steps.instructions: With the bed unoccupied and positioned safely: Connect the bed to verified AC power. Test basic frame functions and controls. Confirm normal AC operation. Disconnect AC power. Observe the transition to battery operation. Test only the functions intended to operate on backup power. Note whether: The bed shuts down immediately. Functions begin and then stop under load. Only one control station is affected. Indicators dim, reset, or behave intermittently. Reconnecting AC immediately restores operation. Expected outcome: The bed transitions to battery operation without an unexpected reset and performs its intended backup-power functions consistently. If operation is stable and repeatable, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Rule Out a Control or Function-Specific Problem
steps.instructions: A reported battery problem may actually be an unrelated control, lockout, actuator, or accessory fault. Test the same function from another available caregiver control. Verify that motion lockouts are not active. Check whether the affected function also fails on AC power. Disconnect only approved external accessories that may be loading the system. Compare operation with a known-good compatible pendant or control accessory when permitted. Expected outcome: The failure is correctly isolated to battery operation rather than a specific control, accessory, lockout, or mechanical function. If the function works normally after correcting the external control or accessory issue, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Inspect for Conditions That Increase Battery Load
steps.instructions: Check for external conditions that may cause excessive demand or repeated operation. A control button held continuously. A damaged pendant activating commands intermittently. An accessory connected to an auxiliary power point. Repeated actuator cycling during testing or transport. A frame component obstructed by bedding, equipment, cables, or the environment. Indicators or accessories remaining active unexpectedly. Expected outcome: No external control, obstruction, or accessory is causing abnormal power demand. If removing the external load restores dependable battery operation, document the cause and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After any correction: Confirm stable operation on verified AC power. Confirm that charging indications are normal. Disconnect AC and verify intended backup-power functions. Operate representative frame movements without a patient. Confirm controls, indicators, brakes, steering, alarms, and emergency functions relevant to safe use. Reconnect AC and verify that charging resumes. Complete electrical safety testing when required by facility policy or after power-system repair. Expected outcome: The bed operates safely on AC, transitions correctly to battery power, performs intended backup functions, and resumes charging when reconnected. If all required checks pass, return the bed to service and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the VersaCare bed operated on AC power but immediately lost powered functions when unplugged.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the bed had been left disconnected from AC power and the battery remained discharged after only a brief charging attempt.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering connected the bed to a verified outlet, allowed an appropriate charging period, and confirmed stable backup-power operation and normal charging before returning it to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact battery, power, or service indication.
Whether the bed operated normally on AC power.
Whether failure occurred immediately or after brief battery use.
Functions tested on AC and battery.
Final electrical safety and device status.

title: Hillrom VersaCare Hospital Bed - Bed Frame Will Not Raise, Lower, Or Articulate
description: Troubleshooting failed bed movement caused by power loss, lockouts, controls, obstructions, overloaded accessories, cable damage, positioning, or actuator-related faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unreliable frame movement while a patient depends on the bed for therapy, positioning, respiratory support, pressure management, or emergency access. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Transfer the patient to another verified bed when required movement cannot be performed safely. Maintain clinically necessary positioning during the exchange. Set the brakes and lower the bed when possible. Support any raised frame section before inspecting beneath or around it. Keep hands, feet, cables, tubing, and equipment away from pinch points. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and no person is exposed to unexpected bed movement or frame collapse. If the bed cannot be placed or maintained in a safe position, remove it from service and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Movement Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The entire bed will not raise or lower. The head, knee, or foot section will not articulate. Movement works from one control station but not another. The motor can be heard but the frame does not move. Movement begins and then stops. The failure occurs only under patient load. The issue is intermittent or direction-specific. The bed displays a power, lockout, or service indication. Expected outcome: The affected movement, control location, direction, and operating condition are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Basic Bed Operation
steps.instructions: Connect the bed directly to a known-good hospital-grade receptacle. Confirm the plug is fully seated. Inspect the power cord and plug for visible damage. Observe normal power indicators. Test an unrelated powered function. If safe, compare operation on AC and backup power. Avoid extension cords and unverified power strips. Expected outcome: The bed has a verified power source and other basic powered functions operate normally. If restoring AC power resolves the movement problem, complete final verification and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Motion Lockouts and Function Restrictions
steps.instructions: Inspect the caregiver controls for active lockouts. Confirm whether the affected movement has been intentionally disabled. Verify that the correct function and direction are selected. Ask clinical staff whether restrictions were applied for patient safety. Remove only unintended lockouts and only when clinically authorized. Do not enter unauthorized configuration or service menus. Expected outcome: The required movement is enabled, or an intentional lockout fully explains the complaint. If removing an unintended lockout restores operation, verify all authorized controls and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Test All Available Control Locations
steps.instructions: Test the affected movement from each approved control location. These may include: Caregiver side-rail controls. Patient side-rail controls. Patient pendant or hand control. Foot-end caregiver controls. Other external controls provided with the bed. Record whether the function fails from all controls or only one. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to one control station or confirmed as a movement-system failure affecting all controls. If another control operates the function normally, troubleshoot the unresponsive control or accessory separately.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Control Cables and External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible control cables and connectors. Look for: Loose or partially engaged connectors. Pinched, stretched, cut, or crushed cables. Cables trapped in side rails or articulation joints. Bent contacts, contamination, corrosion, or broken retaining features. Damage caused by transport, cleaning, or mattress replacement. Reseat approved accessible connectors without forcing them, and route cables away from moving sections. Expected outcome: External control connections are secure, undamaged, and correctly routed. If reseating or rerouting a connection restores movement, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for Physical Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect the full movement path before operating the frame. Look for: Bedding, mattress retainers, linens, or patient-positioning devices trapped in the frame. Power cords, nurse-call cables, tubing, or accessory cables crossing moving joints. Overbed tables, walls, furniture, lifts, or equipment blocking travel. Accessories mounted incorrectly or contacting the frame. Objects stored under the bed. A frame section already at its mechanical endpoint. Expected outcome: The movement path is clear and no external object prevents articulation. If removing the obstruction restores normal motion, inspect for damage and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Reduce External Load and Check Accessory Placement
steps.instructions: With the patient safely transferred when necessary: Remove nonessential equipment attached to the moving frame section. Confirm accessories are mounted in approved locations. Check for excessive loading from pumps, monitors, traction equipment, or storage. Verify the mattress and surface are correctly positioned. Confirm no accessory cable becomes taut during movement. Do not exceed manufacturer loading requirements; consult current Hillrom documentation when limits must be verified. Expected outcome: The bed moves normally without an improperly placed accessory or external load restricting operation. If correcting accessory placement restores movement, complete final verification and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Observe the Failure Without Disassembly
steps.instructions: With the bed unoccupied and the movement path clear, command the affected function briefly. Observe whether: There is no sound or response. A motor or actuator sound is present. The section moves slowly, unevenly, or intermittently. Movement stops when the cable or frame position changes. The opposite direction works. Another section moves unexpectedly. There is grinding, binding, clicking, overheating, odor, or visible deformation. Stop immediately if abnormal sound, heat, odor, binding, or unintended movement occurs. Expected outcome: The symptom is safely characterized without opening the bed or accessing internal components. If abnormal mechanical behavior is present, remove the bed from service and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Compare With a Known-Good Accessory or Bed
steps.instructions: When available: Test with a known-good compatible pendant or hand control. Compare lockout indications and control behavior with another VersaCare bed. Compare normal sound and movement characteristics without using the other bed as a source of undocumented specifications. Do not exchange actuators, internal cables, control boards, or other service components without an approved procedure. Expected outcome: The comparison helps distinguish an accessory or operating-condition problem from a bed-level fault. If a known-good accessory resolves the issue, replace the defective accessory and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 11. Verify Emergency and Manual Functions
steps.instructions: Where relevant, confirm that emergency or manually operated functions are accessible and behave normally. Do not activate emergency functions unnecessarily with a patient in the bed. Follow facility procedures and current manufacturer instructions. Confirm that any emergency release is fully reset after testing. Do not use an emergency release as a substitute for repairing failed powered articulation. Expected outcome: Emergency provisions remain available and are not causing or masking the powered-movement failure. If an improperly reset external release caused the problem and normal operation is restored, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction and with the bed unoccupied: Test bed raise and lower through a safe operating range. Test head, knee, and foot articulation. Test each available control station. Confirm lockouts disable only the intended functions. Observe smooth motion without binding, unusual sound, hesitation, or drift. Verify controls stop movement immediately when released. Confirm cables remain clear throughout articulation. Verify brakes, side rails, alarms, indicators, and emergency functions relevant to safe use. Complete electrical safety testing when required after repair. Expected outcome: All required frame movements operate smoothly and consistently from authorized controls without obstruction, abnormal behavior, or unintended motion. If all checks pass, return the bed to service and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the VersaCare bed would not raise or lower from the patient pendant or side-rail controls.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the bed-height motion lockout unintentionally enabled at the caregiver control panel.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the unintended lockout with clinical approval and verified bed height and articulation functions from all control locations before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether a motor or actuator sound was present.
Unusual sound, heat, odor, binding, or damage.
Final functional and electrical safety status.

title: Hillrom VersaCare Hospital Bed - Brake Or Steering Mechanism Failure
description: Troubleshooting brake or steering problems caused by pedal position, caster obstruction, debris, floor conditions, linkage issues, damage, or incorrect operation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Unintended Movement
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable brake or steering system while the bed is being used for patient entry, exit, transfer, transport, or repositioning. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Transfer the patient to another verified bed when practical. If immediate transfer is unsafe, keep staff with the patient and prevent bed movement. Use approved wheel chocks or another facility-approved method only when necessary for temporary stabilization. Do not rely on a questionable brake to secure an occupied bed. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from falls, collisions, and unexpected bed movement. If the bed cannot be stabilized safely, remove it from service immediately and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
