steps.instructions: Determine whether: The brake pedal will not move into the brake position. The pedal moves, but one or more casters still roll. The bed rolls despite the brake appearing engaged. The steering function does not guide the bed. The bed is difficult to push or pulls to one side. The pedal is loose, bent, binding, or does not remain in position. The problem occurs on all floor surfaces or only in one location. A brake warning remains active after engagement, if equipped. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as a pedal, braking, steering, caster, warning, or environmental problem.

steps.title: 3. Remove External Loads and Obstructions
steps.instructions: With the bed unoccupied and safely stabilized: Remove equipment, cables, linens, or accessories contacting the floor. Confirm no power cord or nurse-call cable is wrapped around a caster. Check for bedding trapped between the frame and wheels. Move portable devices, furniture, and wall-mounted equipment away from the bed. Confirm the bed is not resting against a threshold, floor transition, or fixed object. Expected outcome: The bed and all casters are free from external obstructions. If removing the obstruction restores normal braking or steering, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Floor and Test Location
steps.instructions: Evaluate the floor where the problem was reported. Look for: Wet, oily, dusty, polished, or contaminated surfaces. Uneven flooring, thresholds, damaged tiles, or slopes. Debris that may prevent caster contact. A surface that is unusually slippery or soft. Construction coverings or floor mats interfering with the casters. Move the unoccupied bed to a clean, level, dry area and repeat the test. Expected outcome: Brake and steering performance is evaluated on a suitable floor surface. If the bed functions normally in the alternate area, address the environmental condition and troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Correct Pedal Position and Operation
steps.instructions: Operate the accessible brake and steering pedals through their normal positions. Confirm the pedal is moved fully into the intended brake, neutral, or steering position. Do not force a pedal that is jammed or unusually resistant. Observe whether the pedal travels evenly and remains in position. Compare pedal position and feel with another verified VersaCare bed when available. Confirm staff were using the correct pedal and position. Expected outcome: The pedal moves smoothly through its normal positions, remains engaged, and is being operated correctly. If correct positioning restores normal operation, complete final verification and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Casters and Accessible Brake Components
steps.instructions: Inspect each caster and all accessible external brake or steering components. Look for: Hair, tape, suture material, plastic, or debris wrapped around the wheel or swivel. Flat spots, cracks, missing tread, or visibly damaged wheels. Bent forks, loose hardware, misaligned casters, or impact damage. A caster that does not swivel or rotate freely in neutral. A visibly damaged or disconnected external linkage. Fluid contamination or corrosion. Do not place hands beneath an unstable bed or near moving linkage while operating pedals. Expected outcome: Casters and external brake components are clean, aligned, secure, and free of visible damage. If debris removal restores operation, proceed to final verification. If damage is present, remove the bed from service.

steps.title: 7. Test Brake Holding Performance
steps.instructions: On a clean, level floor with the bed unoccupied: Place the pedal fully in the brake position. Apply controlled push and pull force from both ends of the bed. Observe each caster for rolling or swiveling. Repeat the test from each side. Release and reapply the brake to confirm repeatability. Do not use excessive force that could overturn equipment or injure personnel. Expected outcome: The bed remains stable, the brake engagement is repeatable, and no caster rolls unexpectedly. If the bed holds securely during repeated testing, troubleshooting can stop after completing steering verification.

steps.title: 8. Test Neutral and Steering Operation
steps.instructions: Release the brake and place the pedal in the appropriate neutral or steering position. Confirm the bed rolls without abnormal drag. Verify that all casters rotate and swivel as intended. Test steering in a clear hallway or approved test area. Observe whether the bed tracks predictably without pulling sharply. Compare operation with a known-good VersaCare bed when available. Confirm accessories or attached equipment are not altering the handling. Expected outcome: The bed rolls freely in neutral and tracks predictably when steering is engaged. If steering operates normally after clearing an external condition, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Brake Warning Behavior When Applicable
steps.instructions: If the complaint includes a brake warning: Engage and release the brake several times. Observe whether the warning follows the actual pedal position. Confirm the bed is connected to normal power. Check for visible damage or obstruction around accessible pedal components. Do not adjust sensors, linkages, or internal switches without the approved manufacturer procedure. Expected outcome: Any brake-status indication accurately matches the physical brake condition. If the warning remains incorrect despite normal pedal operation, remove the bed from service for service-level evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Test brake engagement several times. Push and pull the bed from multiple directions. Confirm neutral rolling. Confirm steering operation and predictable tracking. Verify all casters rotate and swivel normally. Check pedal stability and return. Confirm any brake warning corresponds to actual brake position. Inspect the power cord and attached cables after moving the bed. Verify safe operation with the bed unloaded before clinical release. Expected outcome: The bed holds securely when braked, rolls freely in neutral, steers predictably, and provides accurate brake status when equipped. If all checks pass, return the bed to service and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the VersaCare bed would not steer properly and pulled sharply to one side during transport.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a nurse-call cable wrapped around a front caster, preventing normal swivel movement.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed and rerouted the cable, inspected the caster, and verified normal neutral rolling, steering, and brake holding performance.

helpfulDetails: Whether brake, neutral, steering, or multiple positions were affected.
Patient occupancy and clinical activity at the time.

title: Hillrom VersaCare Hospital Bed - Patient Pendant Or Hand Control Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting an unresponsive pendant or hand control caused by lockouts, loose connections, cable damage, contamination, incorrect operation, or accessory failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable pendant while a patient depends on it for positioning, communication, lighting, or other accessible functions. Notify the responsible clinical staff. Use verified caregiver controls when safe and available. Transfer the patient to another verified bed if necessary functions cannot be controlled reliably. Place the bed in a safe position and set the brakes. Keep the pendant within the patientâ€™s reach only after reliable operation is confirmed. Expected outcome: The patient has a dependable alternate method for required bed functions and is not relying on an unresponsive control. If safe control cannot be maintained, remove the bed from clinical use and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The entire pendant is unresponsive. Only one button or function fails. The problem is intermittent. The pendant works only when the cable is moved. Caregiver controls continue to work. The issue began after cleaning, transport, bed movement, or accessory replacement. A lockout or disabled-function indicator is present. Expected outcome: The failure is defined as a complete pendant failure, isolated button failure, function lockout, connection issue, or broader bed-control problem.

steps.title: 3. Verify Bed Power and Basic Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the bed is connected to a verified AC source and shows normal power indications. Test a basic bed function from the caregiver control panel. Confirm whether the bed responds from any other control location. Check whether the failure continues on both AC and battery power when safe to test. If all controls are unresponsive, treat the issue as a bed power or control-system problem rather than only a pendant problem. Expected outcome: The bed is powered and responds normally from at least one other control location. If restoring bed power resolves the pendant complaint, complete final verification and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Control Lockouts and Enabled Functions
steps.instructions: Inspect the caregiver controls for active lockouts or function restrictions. Confirm the reported function has not been intentionally disabled. Verify that the control is being used within its permitted operating condition. Ask clinical staff whether lockouts were activated for patient safety. Do not defeat a clinically required lockout without authorization. Do not access unauthorized configuration or service menus. Expected outcome: Required pendant functions are enabled, or an intentional lockout fully explains the complaint. If removing an unintended lockout restores normal operation, verify all authorized controls and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Pendant and Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the pendant housing and the full accessible cable length. Look for: Cracks, missing buttons, damaged overlays, or loose housing sections. Fluid intrusion, dried residue, or contamination around buttons. Cuts, pinches, stretching, kinks, exposed conductors, or crushed cable sections. Damage caused by side rails, frame articulation, wheels, or mattress movement. A cable pulled tightly or routed through a moving joint. Do not use a damaged pendant in patient care. Expected outcome: The pendant and cable are clean, intact, flexible, and free of damage or entrapment. If physical damage is found, replace the approved accessory or remove the bed from service as appropriate. Troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect and Reseat the Accessible Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect power when required by the approved connection procedure. Locate the externally accessible pendant connection. Inspect the connector shell, alignment, retaining feature, and visible contacts. Check for looseness, contamination, corrosion, bent contacts, or broken locking features. Reconnect the pendant fully without forcing it. Route the cable to prevent pulling, pinching, or contact with moving bed sections. Expected outcome: The pendant connection is fully seated, retained, clean, and properly routed. If reseating the connection restores reliable operation, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Test Each Pendant Function Methodically
steps.instructions: With the bed unoccupied or with the patient safely transferred: Test each pendant button individually. Observe whether indicators illuminate or commands are acknowledged. Verify that commands stop when the button is released. Confirm that no button is stuck, delayed, or intermittently active. Compare pendant commands with the same functions from the caregiver controls. Expected outcome: Each enabled pendant command operates consistently and stops immediately when released. If all functions operate correctly and repeatably, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Pendant
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility procedure, connect a known-good, compatible Hillrom pendant or hand control. Confirm compatibility before connection. Do not use an unapproved accessory. Test the same functions under the same conditions. If the known-good pendant works, retest the original pendant to confirm the result. If neither pendant works, continue evaluating the bed-side connection and control system. Expected outcome: The substitution isolates the issue to the original pendant or confirms that the problem remains with the bed. If the known-good pendant resolves the issue, replace the defective accessory and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Check for Mechanical or Function-Specific Conditions
steps.instructions: A pendant may be sending a valid command while the requested bed function is blocked. Confirm the frame section is not at its travel endpoint. Remove bedding, cables, equipment, or environmental obstructions. Confirm the bed is not against a wall or fixed object. Check whether the same function fails from caregiver controls. Verify that no emergency release or mechanical condition is preventing powered movement. Expected outcome: No obstruction, endpoint condition, lockout, or mechanical problem is being mistaken for pendant failure. If removing the external obstruction restores the function, verify safe operation and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Test all pendant buttons and enabled functions. Test corresponding caregiver controls. Confirm that commands begin and stop correctly. Flex the cable gently during testing to identify intermittent faults. Verify proper cable routing through the bedâ€™s full safe articulation range. Confirm the pendant can be stored and reached safely. Check nurse-call, lighting, or entertainment functions when included and connected. Confirm no unintended movement or stuck command occurs. Expected outcome: The pendant operates every enabled function consistently, the cable remains secure during articulation, and no unintended command occurs. If all checks pass, return the bed or accessory to service and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the patient hand control would not operate the head or knee sections, although caregiver controls remained functional.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the pendant connector partially disengaged and the cable pulled tightly around the side rail.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and secured the connector, rerouted the cable, and verified all pendant and caregiver-control functions through bed articulation.

helpfulDetails: Evidence of fluid or cleaning residue.
